modelEssay.title: Why Students Should Be Encouraged to Develop Creativity
modelEssay.content:
In an era where innovation is the key to progress, fostering creativity in students is of paramount importance. Firstly, creativity equips students with the ability to think critically and solve problems in novel ways, which is essential in a rapidly changing world. Moreover, creative individuals are more likely to contribute to society by generating new ideas and approaches to existing challenges.

In addition to these benefits, creativity also enhances personal development. Students who are encouraged to be creative tend to be more confident and adaptable, as they learn to trust their own ideas and abilities. Furthermore, creativity can lead to a more fulfilling educational experience, as it allows students to explore their interests and passions.

In conclusion, nurturing creativity in students is crucial for their future success and the advancement of society. Schools and educators should prioritize the development of creative thinking skills, providing students with opportunities to engage in creative activities and express their unique perspectives.

structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：阐述创造力对学生个人发展和社会贡献的益处
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：强调培养学生创造力的重要性，并提出教育者应采取的措施

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我能记录一些信息以协助我查看您的索赔吗？

transcript.text: It's Miss May Wilson of 15 South C Road in Cornwall, and the details are that our village was extensively flooded two months ago.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我是梅·威尔逊小姐，地址是康沃尔郡南C路15号。情况是两个月前我们村庄遭受了大面积洪灾。

transcript.text: The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们小屋的整个一楼都被水淹没了。

transcript.text: And five of us have been living in a caravan ever since.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 从那以后，我们五个人一直住在一辆活动房车上。

transcript.text: You people are still withholding the money we are entitled to over a bizarre technical detail, and it's not acceptable, Paul.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你们这些人却因为一个离奇的技术细节，仍然扣着我们有权获得的钱不给，这让人无法接受，保罗。

transcript.text: Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 威尔逊小姐，根据您账户上的记录，您提到的那个离奇的技术细节指的是，事发前一个月您没有缴纳房屋保险费。

transcript.text: That money left our account, and now that you should be paying out, you are suddenly saying that you didn't receive it on time.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那笔钱已经从我们账户划走了，而现在到了你们该赔付的时候，你们却突然说没有按时收到这笔钱。

transcript.text: I'm really sceptical about this claim.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我对此深表怀疑。

transcript.text: The contract does say that any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract and may affect claims.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 合同上确实说明，一年内任何一次未缴款都会影响保险合同的条款和条件，并可能影响索赔。

transcript.text: Of course, I can pass you on to my manager to talk to you more about this.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 当然，我可以将您转接给我的经理，让他与您进一步讨论此事。

transcript.text: I've already spoken to him, and you can tell him I'm furious now and that your company has a lawsuit on its hands.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: You will be hearing from my lawyer.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你会收到我律师的函件。

transcript.text: Goodbye.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 再见。

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话2。

transcript.text: How do you feel about the future of artificial intelligence?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你对人工智能的未来有何看法？

transcript.text: Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 就我个人而言，我对此相当乐观。

transcript.text: AI?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人工智能？

transcript.text: I'm not so optimistic, actually.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 实际上，我不那么乐观。

transcript.text: In fact, it's something we should be concerned about.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 事实上，这是我们应该担心的事情。

transcript.text: Well, it will help us humans understand ourselves better.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，它将帮助我们人类更好地了解自己。

transcript.text: And when we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can improve the world.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 而当我们更好地了解自己时，我们可以改善世界。

transcript.text: Well, one thing is for sure.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，有一件事是肯定的。

transcript.text: Technology is evolving faster than our ability to understand it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 技术的发展速度超过了我们理解它的能力。

transcript.text: And in the future, AI will make jobs kind of pointless.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在未来，人工智能会让工作变得有点无意义。

transcript.text: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time, and allow us to be centered on creative tasks.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我认为人工智能实际上会帮助创造新型工作，这些工作需要的时间更少，并让我们专注于创造性任务。

transcript.text: I doubt that very much.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我非常怀疑这一点。

transcript.text: Probably the last job that will remain will be writing AI software.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 可能最后剩下的工作将是编写人工智能软件。

transcript.text: And then eventually, AI will just write its own software.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 然后最终，人工智能将自己编写自己的软件。

transcript.text: At that time, we are going to have a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 到那时，我们将有很多没人愿意做的工作。

transcript.text: So we'll need artificial intelligence for the robots to take care of the old guys like us.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以我们需要人工智能让机器人照顾像我们这样的老人。

transcript.text: I don't know.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我不知道。

transcript.text: There's a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 有一种风险是，人类文明可能被一种更高级的数字生命所取代。

transcript.text: AI will be able to completely simulate a person in every way possible.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人工智能将能够完全模拟一个人，以所有可能的方式。

transcript.text: In fact, some people think we're in a simulation right now.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 事实上，有些人认为我们现在就在模拟中。

transcript.text: That's impossible.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那不可能。

transcript.text: Humans can't even make a mosquito.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人类甚至造不出一只蚊子。

transcript.text: Computers only have chips.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 计算机只有芯片。

transcript.text: People have brains, and that's where the wisdom comes from.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人们有大脑，智慧就来源于此。

transcript.text: Once it's fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 一旦完全发展，人工智能会厌倦尝试与人类沟通，因为相比之下，我们的思维要慢得多。

transcript.text: I'm not so sure.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我不太确定。

transcript.text: A computer is a computer, and a computer is just a toy.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 计算机就是计算机，计算机只是一个玩具。

transcript.text: Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 计算机可以轻松地进行极其快速的通信。

transcript.text: So the computer will just get impatient talking to humans.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以计算机在与人类交谈时会变得不耐烦。

transcript.text: It'll be barely getting any information out.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 它几乎得不到任何信息。

transcript.text: Well, I believe there's a benevolent future with AI.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，我相信人工智能有一个仁慈的未来。

transcript.text: I also think you watch too many science fiction films.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我也认为你看太多科幻电影了。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 文章一。

transcript.text: To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
transcript.translation: 要实现财务安全，你储蓄的金额永远比你赚多少钱或投资多精明更重要。

transcript.text: If you're under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
transcript.translation: 如果你不到30岁，你的目标应该是每月储蓄税后收入的20%。

transcript.text: This is irrespective of how much you earn.
transcript.translation: 这与你的收入多少无关。

transcript.text: Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
transcript.translation: 大约50%应预留用于食物和住房等基本开支。

transcript.text: The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
transcript.translation: 剩下的30%用于休闲娱乐。

transcript.text: But for many young people, it'll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
transcript.translation: 但对许多年轻人来说，将如此大比例的收入指定用于储蓄是困难的。

transcript.text: If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending.
transcript.translation: 如果你觉得存钱很难，那就从削减所有不必要的开支开始。

transcript.text: Allocate a tiny amount of 1 or 2 % for savings and gradually increase that amount.
transcript.translation: 先分配一小笔1%或2%用于储蓄，并逐渐增加这个金额。

transcript.text: Always keep that 20% goal in mind to prevent yourself from becoming complacent.
transcript.translation: 要始终牢记20%的目标，以防自己变得自满。

transcript.text: It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan.
transcript.translation: 坚持这样一个严格的计划可能具有挑战性。

transcript.text: But if you adopt the right mindset, you should be able to make it work for you.
transcript.translation: 但如果你采取正确的心态，你应该能让它为你所用。

transcript.text: So what should you be doing with the money that you're saving?
transcript.translation: 那么，你应该用你存下来的钱做什么呢？

transcript.text: Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
transcript.translation: 一部分必须保持易于取用，以备紧急需要现金。

transcript.text: The largest proportion should be invested in retirement plans, either through your employer or privately.
transcript.translation: 最大比例应投资于退休计划，无论是通过你的雇主还是私下进行。

transcript.text: And you can keep some money for high-risk but potentially lucrative investments.
transcript.translation: 并且你可以保留一些钱用于高风险但可能带来丰厚回报的投资。

transcript.text: Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
transcript.translation: 股息可以再投资，或用于购买你喜欢的东西。

transcript.text: By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now and still be financially secure in the future.
transcript.translation: 遵循这个计划，你应该有望既能享受当下的生活，又能确保未来的财务安全。

transcript.translation: 但没有人能每天都穿着独特的服装。

transcript.text: I mean, that's why uniforms were invented.

transcript.text: I created my own uniform.
transcript.translation: 我创造了自己的制服。

transcript.text: To do this, I chose an appropriate outfit.
transcript.translation: 为此，我选择了一套合适的服装。

transcript.text: Then I bought multiple items of the same style in different shades.
transcript.translation: 然后我买了多件相同风格但不同色调的衣服。

transcript.text: Now, I never worry about what I'm wearing in the morning, even if I do get a bit tired of just wearing the same classic pieces.
transcript.translation: 现在，我从不担心早上穿什么，即使我确实有点厌倦只穿同样的经典款式。

transcript.text: Overall, when it comes to work, you have to ask yourself, would looking smarter enhance my ability to do my job?
transcript.translation: 总的来说，当涉及到工作时，你必须问自己，看起来更聪明会提升我的工作能力吗？

transcript.text: For some, this question may not be an issue at all, especially if you work remotely and rarely see your colleagues or clients face-to-face.
transcript.translation: 对某些人来说，这可能根本不是问题，尤其是如果你远程工作，很少与同事或客户面对面见面。

transcript.text: But if your job involves interacting with other people, the answer to this is often yes.
transcript.translation: 但如果你的工作涉及与其他人互动，答案通常是肯定的。

transcript.text: So, rather than fighting the system, I think we should just do whatever helps us to achieve our goals at work.
transcript.translation: 所以，我认为与其对抗这个体系，我们不如做任何有助于实现工作目标的事情。

transcript.text: If that means playing it safe with your image, then let's face it, it's probably worth it.
transcript.translation: 如果这意味着在形象上保持稳妥，那么面对现实吧，这可能是值得的。

transcript.text: Did you know that Americans have approximately three times the amount of space we had 50 years ago?
transcript.translation: 你知道吗，美国人拥有的空间大约是50年前的三倍？

transcript.text: Therefore, you'd think we'd have sufficient room for all of our possessions.
transcript.translation: 因此，你会认为我们有足够空间存放所有物品。

transcript.text: On the contrary, the personal storage business is now a growing industry.
transcript.translation: 相反，个人储物业务现在是一个增长中的行业。

transcript.text: We've got triple the space, but we've become such enthusiastic consumers that we require even more.
transcript.translation: 我们有了三倍的空间，但我们已成为如此热情的消费者，以至于我们需要更多。

transcript.text: This phenomenon has resulted in significant credit card debt, enormous environmental footprints, and perhaps not coincidentally, our happiness levels have failed to increase over the same half-century.
transcript.translation: 这一现象导致了显著的信用卡债务、巨大的环境足迹，或许并非巧合，我们的幸福水平在同一半个世纪里未能提升。

transcript.text: I'm here to suggest an alternative that having less might actually be a preferable decision.
transcript.translation: 我在此提出一个替代方案，即拥有更少可能实际上是一个更可取的决定。

transcript.text: Many of us have experienced at some stage, the pleasure of possessing less.
transcript.translation: 我们许多人在某个阶段都体验过拥有更少的快乐。

transcript.text: I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economise, but also simplify your life.
transcript.translation: 我提议，更少的东西和更少的空间不仅能帮你节省开支，还能简化你的生活。

transcript.text: I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
transcript.translation: 我最近开始了一个创新项目，以发现一些能提供我所需一切的创意解决方案。

transcript.text: By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square metres instead of 60, I immediately saved $200 ,000.
transcript.translation: 通过购买一套40平方米而非60平方米的公寓，我立即节省了20万美元。

transcript.text: Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills and also a smaller carbon footprint.
transcript.translation: 更小的空间导致更低的水电费账单，以及更小的碳足迹。

transcript.text: Because it's designed around an edited collection of possessions, limited to my favourite stuff, I'm really excited to live there.
transcript.translation: 因为它是围绕一个精选的物品收藏设计的，仅限于我最喜欢的东西，我真的很兴奋住在那里。

transcript.text: How can we live more basically?
transcript.translation: 我们如何能更基本地生活？

transcript.text: Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
transcript.translation: 首先，我们必须无情地将不必要的物品从生活中剔除。

transcript.text: To stem consumption, we should think before we buy and ask ourselves, will it truly make me happier?
transcript.translation: 为了抑制消费，我们应该在购买前思考，并问自己，它真的会让我更快乐吗？

transcript.text: Obviously, we should possess some great stuff, but we want belongings that we're going to love for years.
transcript.translation: 显然，我们应该拥有一些好东西，但我们想要的是我们会长期喜爱的物品。

transcript.text: Secondly, we require space efficiency.
transcript.translation: 其次，我们需要空间效率。

transcript.text: We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
transcript.translation: 我们想要的是设计用于大部分时间使用的电器，而不是偶尔使用的。

transcript.text: Why own a six-burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
transcript.translation: 为什么拥有一个六灶头的炉子，而你很少使用甚至三个灶头？

transcript.text: Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.
transcript.translation: 最后，我们需要多功能空间和家居用品。

transcript.text: I combined a movable wall with transforming furniture to get more out of my limited space.
transcript.translation: 我将移动墙与变形家具结合起来，以充分利用有限空间。

transcript.text: Consider my coffee table.
transcript.translation: 考虑一下我的咖啡桌。

transcript.text: It increases in size to accommodate 10.
transcript.translation: 它可以扩大尺寸以容纳10人。

transcript.text: My office is tucked away, easily hidden.
transcript.translation: 我的办公室被隐藏起来，易于隐藏。

transcript.text: My bed simply pops out of the wall.
transcript.translation: 我的床直接从墙里弹出来。

transcript.text: For guests, I can relocate the movable wall and utilise the foldable guest beds I installed.
transcript.translation: 对于客人，我可以重新定位移动墙，并利用我安装的折叠客床。

transcript.text: I'm not saying we should all live in tiny apartments, but consider the benefits of an edited life.
transcript.translation: 我并不是说我们都应该住在小公寓里，但考虑一下精选生活的好处。

transcript.text: When you return home and walk through your front door, take a moment to ask yourselves, could I do with a little live editing?
transcript.translation: 当你回到家，走进前门时，花点时间问自己，我是否可以进行一点生活编辑？

transcript.text: Would that give me more freedom and more time?
transcript.translation: 那会给我更多自由和时间吗？

transcript.text: Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation, even if it hurts them to do so.
transcript.translation: 信不信由你，人们有时会为了保持良好、诚实的声誉而撒谎，即使这样做会伤害他们自己。

transcript.text: At least, this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
transcript.translation: 至少，这是一个科学家团队提出的观点，并有证据支持。

transcript.text: Picture this scenario.
transcript.translation: 想象一下这个场景。

transcript.text: You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
transcript.translation: 你经常因工作开车，每月最多可报销400英里。

transcript.text: Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month, but this month you drove 400 miles.
transcript.translation: 你公司的大多数人每月开车约300英里，但这个月你开了400英里。

transcript.text: How many miles do you think you'd claim in your expense report?
transcript.translation: 你认为你会在费用报告中申报多少英里？

transcript.text: The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we're discussing today, with surprising results.
transcript.translation: 科学家在我们今天讨论的研究中提出了这个确切的问题，结果令人惊讶。

transcript.text: They found that 12% of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
transcript.translation: 他们发现12%的受访者报告的行驶距离低于实际数字，平均答案为384英里。

transcript.text: In other words, they lied about the number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
transcript.translation: 换句话说，他们谎报了英里数，即使这会使他们损失应得的钱。

transcript.text: The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high-expense claim.
transcript.translation: 研究人员认为这是为了显得诚实，假设是他人会对高额费用申报持怀疑态度。

transcript.text: But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
transcript.translation: 但为什么人们会编造数字来损害自己的利益呢？

transcript.text: The researchers explain that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they'll be judged by others.
transcript.translation: 研究人员解释说，许多人非常关心自己的声誉以及他人如何评判他们。

transcript.text: If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
transcript.translation: 如果他们足够关心，他们对显得诚实而不失去他人尊重的担忧可能超过他们实际诚实的欲望。

transcript.text: The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people's suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
transcript.translation: 研究人员断言，研究结果表明，当人们获得非常有利的结果时，他们会预期他人的怀疑反应，宁愿撒谎显得诚实，也不愿说实话而被视为自私的骗子。

transcript.text: So why is this research important?
transcript.translation: 那么为什么这项研究重要呢？

transcript.text: Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie, selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others.
transcript.translation: 嗯，专家们普遍同意有两种主要类型的谎言：自私的谎言和为了利益他人的谎言。

transcript.text: The first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company, while the second involves lying to help others or not offend others.
transcript.translation: 第一种，如你所料，是为了自私的利益，例如向保险公司提交欺诈性索赔；而第二种涉及为了帮助他人或不冒犯他人而撒谎。

transcript.text: For example, telling a friend whose outfit you don't like that they look great.
transcript.translation: 例如，告诉一个你不喜欢其着装的朋友他们看起来很棒。

transcript.text: But the researchers are suggesting a third type of lying, lying to maintain a good reputation.
transcript.translation: 但研究人员提出了第三种类型的撒谎：为了维护良好声誉而撒谎。

transcript.text: Now, this hypothesis is new, and some skeptics argue that this isn't a whole new category of lie, but the findings seem intuitive to me.
transcript.translation: 现在，这个假设是新的，一些怀疑论者认为这并不是一个全新的谎言类别，但对我来说，这些发现似乎很直观。

transcript.text: After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others.
transcript.translation: 毕竟，撒谎的主要动机之一是增加我们在他人眼中的价值。

transcript.text: So it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.
transcript.translation: 因此，人们为了显得诚实而撒谎的可能性很高。

transcript.text: Why do old people dislike new music?
transcript.translation: 为什么老年人不喜欢新音乐？

transcript.text: As I've grown older, I often hear people my age say things like they just don't make good music like they used to.
transcript.translation: 随着年龄增长，我经常听到同龄人说类似的话，比如他们只是不再像过去那样制作好音乐了。

transcript.text: Why does this happen?
transcript.translation: 为什么会这样？

transcript.text: Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
transcript.translation: 幸运的是，心理学可以为我们提供一些对这个谜题的见解。

transcript.text: Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14, and by the time we're in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
transcript.translation: 音乐品味早在13或14岁就开始形成，到20岁出头时，这些品味就相当牢固地固定下来。

transcript.text: In fact, studies have found that by the time we turn 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
transcript.translation: 事实上，研究发现，到我们33岁时，大多数人已经停止听新音乐。

transcript.text: Meanwhile, popular songs released when you're in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group for the rest of your life.
transcript.translation: 同时，你在青少年早期流行的歌曲很可能在你一生中在同龄群体中保持相当流行。

transcript.text: There could be a biological explanation for this, as there's evidence that the brain's ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms, and melodies deteriorates with age.
transcript.translation: 这可能有生物学解释，因为有证据表明，大脑在区分不同和弦、节奏和旋律方面的能力随着年龄增长而衰退。

transcript.text: So to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all sound the same.
transcript.translation: 所以对老年人来说，较新的、不太熟悉的歌曲可能听起来都一样。

transcript.text: But there may be some simpler reasons for older people's aversion to newer music.
transcript.translation: 但老年人对新音乐的厌恶可能有一些更简单的原因。

transcript.text: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the mere exposure effect, which in essence means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
transcript.translation: 社会心理学中研究最多的定律之一叫做单纯曝光效应，本质上意味着我们接触某物越多，就越倾向于喜欢它。

transcript.text: This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see, and the songs we listen to.
transcript.translation: 这种情况发生在我们认识的人、我们看到的广告和我们听的歌曲上。

transcript.text: When you're in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos.
transcript.translation: 当你在青少年早期时，你可能花相当多的时间听音乐或看音乐视频。

transcript.text: Your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
transcript.translation: 你最喜欢的歌曲和艺术家成为你日常生活中熟悉、令人安慰的部分。

transcript.text: For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase.
transcript.translation: 对于许多30岁以上的人来说，工作和家庭责任增加。

transcript.text: So there's less time to spend discovering new music.
transcript.translation: 所以用于发现新音乐的时间就更少了。

transcript.text: Instead, many will simply listen to old, familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
transcript.translation: 相反，许多人只会听那个有更多空闲时间的时期的老旧、熟悉的最爱歌曲。

transcript.text: Of course, those teen years weren't necessarily carefree.
transcript.translation: 当然，那些青少年岁月不一定无忧无虑。

transcript.text: They're famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.

questionGroups.title: Why lifelong learning is the international passport to success

material.title: Why lifelong learning is the international passport to success

paragraphs.text: Picture yourself at a college graduation day, with a fresh cohort (一群) of students about to set sail for new horizons. What are they thinking while they throw their caps in the air? What is it with this thin sheet of paper that makes it so precious? It's not only the proof of acquired knowledge but plays into the reputation game of where you were trained. Being a graduate from Harvard Law School carries that extra glamour, doesn't it? Yet take a closer look, and the diploma is the perfect ending to the modern tragedy of education.
paragraphs.translation: 想象一下你在一个大学毕业典礼上，一群即将启航探索新天地的学生。当他们将帽子抛向空中时，他们在想什么？这张薄纸为何如此珍贵？它不仅是所获知识的证明，还关乎你受教育之处的声誉博弈。成为哈佛法学院的毕业生会带来额外的光彩，不是吗？然而，仔细审视，文凭是现代教育悲剧的完美结局。

paragraphs.text: Why? Because universities and curricula are designed along the three units of French classical tragedy: time, action, and place. Students meet at the university campus (unity of place) for classes (unity of action) during their 20s (unity of time). This classical model has traditionally produced prestigious universities, but it is now challenged by the digitalisation of society—which allows everybody who is connected to the internet to access learning—and by the need to acquire skills in step with a fast-changing world. Universities must realise that learning in your 20s won't be enough. If technological diffusion and implementation develop faster, workers will have to constantly refresh their skills.
paragraphs.translation: 为什么？因为大学和课程设计遵循法国古典悲剧的三个单元：时间、行动和地点。学生在大学校园（地点的统一）上课（行动的统一），年龄在20多岁（时间的统一）。这种传统模式曾产生知名大学，但现在受到社会数字化的挑战——它让所有连接互联网的人都能获取学习机会——以及需要跟上快速变化的世界技能。大学必须意识到，仅在20多岁学习是不够的。如果技术传播和实施发展得更快，工作者将必须不断更新技能。

paragraphs.text: The university model needs to evolve. It must equip students with the right skills and knowledge to compete in a world 'where value will be derived largely from human interaction and the ability to invent and interpret things that machines cannot', as the English futurist Richard Watson puts it. By teaching foundational knowledge and up-to-date skills, universities will provide students with the future-proof skills of lifelong learning, not just get them 'job-ready'.
paragraphs.translation: 大学模式需要进化。它必须赋予学生正确的技能和知识，以在一个'价值将主要来源于人类互动以及发明和解释机器无法处理的事物的能力'的世界中竞争，正如英国未来学家Richard Watson所言。通过教授基础知识和最新技能，大学将为学生提供未来-proof的终身学习技能，而不仅仅是让他们'工作-ready'。

paragraphs.text: Some universities already play a critical role in lifelong learning as they want to keep the value of their diplomas. This new role comes with a huge set of challenges, and needs largely to be invented. One way to start this transformation process could be to go beyond the 'five-year diploma model' to adapt curricula to lifelong learning. We call this model the lifelong passport.
paragraphs.translation: 一些大学已经在终身学习中扮演关键角色，因为他们想保持文凭的价值。这个新角色带来了一系列巨大的挑战，很大程度上需要被创造。启动这一转型过程的一种方式可能是超越'五年文凭模式'，使课程适应终身学习。我们称这种模式为终身护照。

paragraphs.text: The Bachelor's degree could be your passport to lifelong learning. For the first few years, students would 'learn to learn' and get endowed with reasoning skills that remain with them for the rest of their lives. For instance, physics allows you to observe and rationalise the world, but also to integrate observations into models and, sometimes, models into theories or laws that can be used to make predictions. Mathematics is the language used to formulate the laws of physics or economy, and to make rigorous computations that turn into predictions. These two disciplines naturally form the foundational pillars of education in technical universities.
paragraphs.translation: 学士学位可以成为你通往终身学习的护照。最初几年，学生将'学习如何学习'，并获得终身伴随的推理能力。例如，物理学允许你观察和理性化世界，但也允许你将观察整合成模型，有时将模型转化为可用于预测的理论或定律。数学是用于表述物理学或经济学定律的语言，并进行严格计算以转化为预测。这两门学科自然构成技术大学教育的基础支柱。

paragraphs.text: Recent advances in computational methods and data science push us into rethinking science and engineering. Computers increasingly become principal actors in leveraging data to formulate questions, which requires radically new ways of reasoning. Therefore, a new discipline blending computer science, programming, statistics and machine learning should be added to the traditional foundational topics of mathematics and physics. These three pillars would allow you to keep learning complex technical subjects all your life because numeracy (计算) is the foundation upon which everything else is eventually built.
paragraphs.translation: 计算方法和数据科学的最新进展推动我们重新思考科学与工程。计算机日益成为利用数据来表述问题的主要行动者，这需要全新的推理方式。因此，一个融合计算机科学、编程、统计学和机器学习的新学科应被添加到数学和物理学的传统基础主题中。这三大支柱将允许你终身学习复杂的技术科目，因为计算能力是最终构建其他一切的基础。

paragraphs.text: According to this new model, the Master of Science (MSc) would become the first stamp in the lifelong learning journey. The MSc curriculum should prepare students for their professional career by allowing them to focus on acquiring practical skills through projects.
paragraphs.translation: 根据这种新模式，理学硕士（MSc）将成为终身学习旅程中的第一个印章。MSc课程应通过让学生专注于通过项目获取实践技能，为他们的职业生涯做准备。

paragraphs.text: Those projects are then interwoven with fast-paced technical modules (模块) learned 'on-the-fly' and 'at will' depending on the nature of the project. If, for instance, your project is developing an integrated circuit, you will have to take a module on advanced concepts in microelectronics. The most critical skills will be developed before the project even starts, in the form of boot camps (短期强化训练), while the rest can be fostered along with the project, putting them to immediate use and thus providing a rich learning context.
paragraphs.translation: 这些项目随后与快速的技术模块交织，根据项目的性质'即兴'和'随意'学习。例如，如果你的项目是开发集成电路，你将需要学习微电子学高级概念的模块。最关键技能将在项目开始前以短期强化训练的形式培养，而其余技能可以随着项目一起培养，立即将其投入应用，从而提供丰富的学习背景。

paragraphs.text: In addition to technical capabilities, the very nature of projects develops social and entrepreneurial skills, such as design thinking, initiative taking, team leading, activity reporting or resource planning. Not only will those skills be actually integrated into the curriculum but they will be very important to have in the future because they are difficult to automate.
paragraphs.translation: 除了技术能力，项目的本质还培养社交和创业技能，如设计思维、主动性、团队领导、活动报告或资源规划。这些技能不仅将被实际整合到课程中，而且在未来非常重要，因为它们难以自动化。

paragraphs.text: After the MSc diploma is earned, there would be many more stamps of lifelong learning over the years. If universities decide to engage in this learning model, they will have to cope with many organisational challenges that might shake their unity of place and action. First, the number of students would be unpredictable. If all of a university's alumni (往届毕业生) were to become students again, the student body would be much bigger than it is now, and it could become unsustainable for the campus in terms of both size and resources. Second, freshly graduated students would mix with professionally experienced ones. This would change the classroom dynamics, perhaps for the best. Project-based learning with a mixed team reflects the reality of the professional world and could therefore be a better preparation for it.
paragraphs.translation: 获得MSc文凭后，多年来将有更多终身学习的印章。如果大学决定采用这种学习模式，他们将不得不应对许多可能动摇其地点和行动统一的组织挑战。首先，学生人数将是不可预测的。如果一所大学的所有往届毕业生都再次成为学生，学生群体将比现在大得多，对于校园在规模和资源上可能变得不可持续。其次，刚毕业的学生将与拥有专业经验的人混合。这可能会改变课堂动态，或许是最好的。基于项目的混合团队学习反映了职业世界的现实，因此可能是更好的准备。

paragraphs.text: Sounds like science fiction? In many countries, part-time studying is not exceptional: on average across OECD countries, part-time students in 2016 represented 20 per cent of enrolment in tertiary education. In many countries, this share is higher and can exceed 40 per cent in Australia, New Zealand and Sweden.
paragraphs.translation: 听起来像科幻小说？在许多国家，兼职学习并不罕见：平均而言，在OECD国家，2016年兼职学生占高等教育入学人数的20%。在许多国家，这一比例更高，在澳大利亚、新西兰和瑞典可能超过40%。

paragraphs.text: If lifelong learning were to become a priority and the new norm, diplomas, just like passports, could be revalidated periodically. A time-determined revalidation would ease administration for everybody. Universities as well as employers and employees would know when they have to retrain. For instance, graduates from the year 2000 would have to come back in 2005.
paragraphs.translation: 如果终身学习成为优先事项和新常态，文凭就像护照一样，可以定期重新验证。时间确定的重新验证将简化每个人的管理。大学以及雇主和雇员将知道他们何时需要再培训。例如，2000年的毕业生将不得不在2005年回来。

paragraphs.text: This could fix the main organisational challenges for the university, but not for the learners, due to lack of time, family obligations or funds. Here, online learning might be an option because it allows you to save your 'travel time', but it has its limits. So far, none of the major employers associated with online learning platforms such as Coursera and Udacity has committed to hire or even interview graduates of their new online programmes.
paragraphs.translation: 这可以解决大学的主要组织挑战，但不能解决学习者的问题，因为缺乏时间、家庭义务或资金。在这里，在线学习可能是一个选项，因为它允许你节省'旅行时间'，但它有限制。迄今为止，与Coursera和Udacity等在线学习平台相关的主要雇主都没有承诺雇佣甚至面试他们新在线项目的毕业生。

paragraphs.text: Even if time were not an issue, who will pay for lifelong learning? That's the eternal debate: should it be the learner's responsibility, that of his employer, or of the state? For example, in Massachusetts, the healthcare professions require continuing education credits, which are carefully evidenced and documented. Yet the same state's lawyers don't require continuing legal education, although most lawyers do participate in it informally. One explanation is that technology is less of a factor in law than it is in healthcare.
paragraphs.translation: 即使时间不是问题，谁将为终身学习买单？这是永恒的争论：应该是学习者的责任、雇主的责任还是国家的责任？例如，在马萨诸塞州，医疗保健专业需要继续教育学分，这些学分有仔细的证据和记录。然而，同州的律师不需要继续法律教育，尽管大多数律师非正式地参与其中。一个解释是，技术在法律中的作用不如在医疗保健中那么重要。

paragraphs.text: Europe has many scenarios, but the French and Swiss ones are interesting to compare. In France, every individual has a right to lifelong learning organised via a personal learning account that is credited as you work. In Switzerland, lifelong learning is a personal responsibility and not a government one. However, employers and the state encourage continuing education either by funding parts of it or by allowing employees to attend it.
paragraphs.translation: 欧洲有许多情景，但法国和瑞士的情况值得比较。在法国，每个人都有权通过个人学习账户进行终身学习，该账户随着工作而积累学分。在瑞士，终身学习是个人责任，而不是政府责任。然而，雇主和国家通过资助部分费用或允许员工参加来鼓励继续教育。

paragraphs.text: Universities have a fundamental role to play in this journey, and higher education is in for a change. Just like classical theatre, the old university model produced talent and value for society. We are not advocating its abolition but rather calling for the adaptation of its characteristics to meet the needs of today.
paragraphs.translation: 大学在这段旅程中扮演着根本性的角色，高等教育即将迎来变革。就像古典戏剧一样，旧的大学模式为社会培养了人才和价值。我们不是在倡导废除它，而是呼吁调整其特点以满足当今的需求。

paragraphs.text: Why does social media trigger feelings of loneliness and inadequacy? Because instead of being real life, it is, for the most part, impression management, a way of marketing yourself, carefully choosing and filtering the pictures and words to put your best face forward.
paragraphs.translation: 社交媒体为何会引发孤独感和不足感？因为它并非真实生活，大部分情况下是印象管理，一种营销自己的方式，精心选择和筛选图片和文字以展现最佳面貌。

paragraphs.text: Online 'friends' made through social media do not follow the normal psychological progression of an interpersonal relationship. You share neither physical time nor emotional conversations over the Internet. You simply communicate photographs and catchy posts to a diverse group of people whom you have 'friended' or 'followed' based on an accidental interaction. This is not to say that your social media friends can't be real friends. They absolutely can, but the two are not synonymous. Generally speaking, there are no unfiltered comments or casually taken photos on our social media pages. And, rightfully so, because it wouldn't feel safe to be completely authentic and vulnerable with some of our 'friends' whom we don't actually know or with whom trust has yet to be built.
paragraphs.translation: 通过社交媒体结交的在线“朋友”并不遵循正常人际关系的心理发展过程。你们既不共享实际相处时间，也不通过互联网进行情感交流。你只是向一群基于偶然互动而“加为好友”或“关注”的多样化人群分享照片和吸引人的帖子。这并不是说你的社交媒体朋友不能成为真正的朋友。他们绝对可以，但两者并非同义。一般来说，我们的社交媒体页面上没有未经过滤的评论或随意拍摄的照片。而且，理应如此，因为与一些我们实际上不认识或尚未建立信任的“朋友”完全真实和展现脆弱是不安全的。

paragraphs.text: Social media can certainly be an escape from the daily grind, but we must be cautioned against the negative effects, such as addiction, on a person's overall psychological well-being.
paragraphs.translation: 社交媒体当然可以成为逃避日常琐碎的一种方式，但我们必须警惕其负面影响，例如成瘾，对个人整体心理健康的影响。

paragraphs.text: As humans, we yearn for social connection. Scrolling (滚动) through pages of pictures and comments, however, does not provide the same degree of fulfillment as face to face interactions do. Also, we tend to idealize others' lives and compare our downfalls to their greatest accomplishments, ending in feelings of loneliness and inadequacy.
paragraphs.translation: 作为人类，我们渴望社交联系。然而，滚动浏览图片和评论页面并不能提供与面对面互动相同程度的满足感。此外，我们倾向于理想化他人的生活，并将我们的失败与他们的最大成就进行比较，最终导致孤独感和不足感。

paragraphs.text: Social media can lead people on the unhealthy quest for perfection. Some people begin to attend certain events or travel to different places so that they can snap that 'perfect' photo. They begin to seek validation through the number of people who 'like' their posts. In order for it to play a psychologically healthy role in your social life, social media should supplement an already healthy social network. Pictures and posts should be byproducts of life's treasured moments and fun times, not the planned and calculated image that one is putting out into cyberspace in an attempt to fill insecurities or unmet needs.
paragraphs.translation: 社交媒体可能导致人们追求不健康的完美主义。有些人开始参加某些活动或前往不同地点，以便拍摄那张“完美”的照片。他们开始通过“点赞”人数来寻求认可。为了让社交媒体在你的社交生活中发挥健康的心理作用，它应该补充已经健康的社交网络。图片和帖子应该是生活中珍贵时刻和乐趣时光的副产品，而不是为了填补不安全感或未满足需求而精心策划并投放到网络空间中的形象。

paragraphs.text: Ultimately, social media has increased our ability to connect with various types of people all over the globe. It has opened doors for businesses and allowed us to stay connected to people whom we may not otherwise get to follow. However, social media should feel like a fun experience, not one that contributes to negative thoughts and feelings. If the latter is the case, increasing face to face time with trusted friends, and minimizing time scrolling online, will prove to be a reminder that your social network is much more rewarding than any 'like,' 'follow' or 'share' can be.
paragraphs.translation: 最终，社交媒体增强了我们与全球各地不同类型人群的联系能力。它为企业打开了大门，并让我们能够与可能无法关注的人保持联系。然而，社交媒体应该是一种有趣的体验，而不是助长负面思想和情感的体验。如果情况是后者，那么增加与信任朋友面对面的时间，并减少在线滚动的时间，将证明你的社交网络比任何“点赞”、“关注”或“分享”都更有价值。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Imagine that an alien species landed on Earth and, through their mere presence, those aliens caused our art to vanish, our music to homogenize, and our technological know-how to disappear. That is effectively what humans have been doing to our closest relatives—chimps (大猩猩).
paragraphs.translation: 设想一个外星物种降落在地球上，并且仅仅通过它们的存在，这些外星人就使我们的艺术消失、我们的音乐同质化、我们的技术知识消失。这实际上就是人类对我们最近的亲属——黑猩猩（大猩猩）一直在做的事情。

paragraphs.text: Back in 1999, a team of scientists led by Andrew Whiten showed that chimps from different parts of Africa behave very differently from one another. Some groups would get each other's attention by rapping branches with their knuckles (指关节) while others did it by loudly ripping leaves with their teeth. The team identified 39 of these traditions that are practiced by some communities but not others—a pattern that, at the time, hadn't been seen in any animal except humans. It was evidence, the team said, that chimps have their own cultures.
paragraphs.translation: 早在1999年，由Andrew Whiten领导的科学家团队表明，来自非洲不同地区的黑猩猩行为差异很大。一些群体通过用指关节敲击树枝来吸引彼此的注意，而其他群体则通过用牙齿大声撕裂叶子来做到这一点。该团队识别了39种这样的传统，这些传统在一些社区中实行，但在其他社区中没有——这种模式在当时除了人类外，在任何动物中都没有见过。团队说，这是黑猩猩拥有自己文化的证据。

paragraphs.text: It took a long time to convince skeptics that such cultures exist, but now we have plenty of examples of animals learning local traditions from one another.
paragraphs.translation: 说服怀疑论者相信这种文化的存在花了很长时间，但现在我们有大量动物从彼此学习当地传统的例子。

paragraphs.text: But just when many scientists have come to accept the existence of animal cultures, many of those cultures might vanish. Ammie Kalan and her colleagues have shown, through years of intensive fieldwork, that the very presence of humans has eroded the diversity of chimp behavior. Where we flourish, their cultures wither. It is a bitterly ironic thing to learn on the 20th anniversary of Whiten's classic study.
paragraphs.translation: 但就在许多科学家开始接受动物文化的存在时，许多这些文化可能正在消失。Ammie Kalan和她的同事通过多年的密集实地调查表明，人类的存在已经侵蚀了黑猩猩行为的多样性。在我们繁荣的地方，它们的文化枯萎。在Whiten经典研究的20周年纪念日了解到这一点，是一件苦涩而讽刺的事情。

paragraphs.text: 'It's amazing to think that just 60 years ago, we knew next to nothing of the behavior of our sister species in the wild,' Whiten says. 'But now, just as we are truly getting to know our primate (灵长类) cousins, the actions of humans are closing the window on all we have discovered.'
paragraphs.translation: ‘想到仅仅60年前，我们对野生姐妹物种的行为几乎一无所知，这令人惊讶，’Whiten说。‘但现在，就在我们真正开始了解我们的灵长类表亲时，人类的行动正在关闭我们所发现的一切的窗口。’

paragraphs.text: 'Sometimes in the rush to conserve the species, I think we forget about the individuals,' says Cat Hobaiter, a professor at the University of St. Andrews. 'Each population, each community, even each generation of chimps is unique. An event might only have a small impact on the total population of chimps, but it may wipe out an entire community—an entire culture. No matter what we do to restore habitat or support population growth, we may never be able to restore that culture.'
paragraphs.translation: ‘有时候在急于保护物种时，我认为我们忘记了个体，’圣安德鲁斯大学教授Cat Hobaiter说。‘每个种群、每个社区，甚至每一代黑猩猩都是独一无二的。一个事件可能对黑猩猩的总种群影响很小，但它可能消灭整个社区——整个文化。无论我们做什么来恢复栖息地或支持种群增长，我们可能永远无法恢复那种文化。’

paragraphs.text: No one knows whether the destruction of chimp culture is getting worse. Few places have tracked chimp behavior over long periods, and those that have are also more likely to have protected their animals from human influence.
paragraphs.translation: 没有人知道黑猩猩文化的破坏是否在加剧。很少有地方长期跟踪黑猩猩的行为，而那些确实跟踪的地方也更可能保护了它们的动物免受人类影响。

paragraphs.text: Obviously conservationists need to think about saving species in a completely new way—by preserving animal traditions as well as bodies and genes. 'Instead of focusing only on the conservation of genetically based entities like species, we now need to also consider culturally based entities,' says Andrew Whiten.
paragraphs.translation: 显然，保护主义者需要以一种全新的方式思考拯救物种——通过保护动物传统以及身体和基因。‘ instead of focusing only on the conservation of genetically based entities like species, we now need to also consider culturally based entities,’Andrew Whiten说。

No matter what we do to restore habitat or support population growth, we may never be able to restore that culture.' 这表明Hobaiter强调保护每个独特的大猩猩群体的重要性。因此，B选项是正确答案。

questionGroups.sourceText: 青藏铁路是世界上最高最长的高原铁路，全长1,956公里，其中有960公里在海拔4,000多米之上，是连接西藏和中国其他地区的第一条铁路。由于铁路穿越世界上最脆弱的生态系统，建成后都采取了生态保护措施，以确保其成为一条"绿色铁路"。青藏铁路大大缩短了去往西藏的旅行时间。更重要的是，它极大地促进了西藏的经济发展，改善了当地居民的生活。铁路开通后，愈来愈多的人选择乘火车前往西藏，这样还有机会欣赏沿线的美景。

answer.modelTranslation: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is the highest and longest plateau railway in the world, spanning 1,956 kilometers, with 960 kilometers above an altitude of over 4,000 meters. It is the first railway connecting Tibet with other parts of China. As the railway traverses the world's most fragile ecosystems, ecological protection measures have been taken after its construction to ensure it becomes a 'green railway'. The Qinghai-Tibet Railway has significantly reduced travel time to Tibet. More importantly, it has greatly promoted Tibet's economic development and improved the lives of local residents. Since the railway's opening, an increasing number of people choose to travel to Tibet by train, which also offers them the opportunity to enjoy the beautiful scenery along the way.
